messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High NotReady spike detected in namespace=inference-pool-usw-2 — 6 nodes NotReady in 2m, 30% pod evictions. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.
ryan: ack oncall here, paging in. seeing 502/503 uptick on dashboards, alert noise from zagg. digging into node list.
sasha: noticed kubelet restarts on a subset — node list: node-usw2-gpu-12, node-usw2-gpu-17, node-usw2-gpu-21 flapping NotReady -> Ready repeatedly.
tariq: probable correlation with recent driver roll we've staged. checking dmesg on node-usw2-gpu-12 now.
ryan: can someone take node-usw2-gpu-21 to cordon/drain so we stop noisy evictions? I'll open traffic fallback to us-east.
kelsey: @ryan on it, cordoning node-usw2-gpu-21 and draining pods (ignore-daemonsets).

kelsey: ```
kubectl cordon node-usw2-gpu-21
kubectl drain node-usw2-gpu-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

infra-bot: Action OK: node node-usw2-gpu-21 cordoned by kelsey at 3932101256.
sasha: dmesg snippet from node-usw2-gpu-12: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU crtc: panic: out of memory while allocating page tables
[ 1234.568000] dockerd: containerd: shim: oom killed process 9876 (triton_server)
[ 1234.569000] kubelet[1]: I0703 12:34:56.123456 kubelet.go:1234] container runtime breakdown: failed to start container: context deadline exceeded
```
tariq: that looks like GPU OOM cascade causing the runtime to misreport -> kubelet crashloop. should we scale up fallback pool and reduce batch size?
ryan: yes. immediate mitigations: 1) scale inference-fallback pool (+50% replicas), 2) update runtime config to cap batch_size to 8 for affected model, 3) route 35% traffic to eu-west until nodes stable. I'll make the routing change.

ryan: ```
# scale fallback pool
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-fallback --replicas=18
# update configmap to lower batch size
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/infer-runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"batch_size":"8"}}'
```

kelsey: scaling fallback pool now. infra-bot shows HPA reacting, new pods scheduling to eu-west and us-east.

infra-bot: HPA: inference-fallback scaled from 12 -> 18 pods over 40s. New pods passing readiness checks.

sasha: also seeing excessive kubelet restart logs referencing nvidia-container-toolkit errors. grabbing kubelet logs and system journal.
tariq: I pulled container logs for the crashing pod -> triton shows repeated allocation errors then segfault. ```
E Triton: failed to reserve memory for tensor - CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E Triton: aborting worker 1
```

ryan: okay, good call. Rolling nodes to previous driver might be necessary, but that's risky during an incident. prefer throttling traffic + scale for now. Also notify customers: partial degraded for inference-usw-2 region.

ops-lead: Customer impact update: ~4.6% increased 5xx across the fleet, latency p50 up +18% for impacted model routes, a small subset of enterprise customers seeing errors. Recommend status page bulletin: "Degraded performance in US-WEST-2 inference pool; automatic mitigation in progress."

kelsey: status page draft posted to #marketing for review. tagging @ops-lead. :loudspeaker: 

sasha: I created an annotation to isolate kernel-version mismatches: nodes affected have kernel 5.15.0-102 vs healthy nodes 5.15.0-88. Possible regression in vendor drivers combined with memory pressure.
tariq: timeline note: driver rollout v525.70 -> v525.84 started 3932098000, ~40% of nodes updated. Flap starts ~3932101200.

ryan: handoff: I'm staying on until stable. @tariq and @sasha continue driver triage. If kubelet crashloops >3 nodes, escalate to infra for emergency rollback.

sasha: running quick healthcheck script across pool to identify nodes with repeated kubelet restarts: ```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw-2 -o name); do kubectl get pod -n kube-system -l component=kubelet -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=$n; done
```

kelsey: Quick update: after scaling and routing changes, error rate dropped from 4.6% -> 1.2% in 7 minutes. latency p50 back to +6%. still seeing flaps on two nodes.

infra-bot: Scheduled job: rollback-driver job queued for node-usw2-gpu-12,node-usw2-gpu-17 at 3932101440 pending approval.

ops-lead: Approve rollback for the two flapping nodes only. Keep staged rollout paused. Post-incident: full postmortem and formal rollback plan.

ryan: approved. tariq, coordinate with infra to run driver rollback on those nodes and re-run soak tests. Also capture heap profiles from triton server for the pods that OOM'd.
tariq: will run rollback and capture logs. hooking up live gdb if needed.

sasha: final note: we observed an emergent backpressure loop where pods evicted -> remaining pods experienced denser batching -> increased GPU memory pressure -> more OOMs. Mitigation successful: reduce batch_size + scale out + temporary routing. Followup action: add automatic per-node GPU memory watermark and pre-emptive eviction to avoid cascade.

ryan: thanks all. I'll file incident ticket, assign owner for postmortem and follow-ups (driver rollback playbook, routing automation for cross-region fallbacks, and per-node GPU health probe). Stand down 3932101308.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. Next update scheduled in 15m or on major status change."
